TWO REWORKS LANDED PAST REFUSALS AND BOTH ARE NOW APPROVED. #2056 post-merge verified clean (all 5 files identical). #2001 (BUG-1291) APPROVED at af49b12b83fc - MY OWN blocking finding, resolved the way the finding asked: as a DECISION, not a sed. The two-space markdown hard line breaks became explicit
, which was one of the two remedies I named. Verified both halves rather than either: git diff --check is now empty AND cat -A confirms "
$" with no residual trailing space - and line 6 (**Related:**) correctly has NO
, because it is the last line before a blank line and never needed one. A uniform
would have been a subtler rendering change; this is line-by-line correct. The substantive code is unchanged from what I already reviewed, established by the stripped +/- method rather than patch-id: ec1333c692 -> 3b490c07f3 and 64e4e5755b -> a4095b80b7 both hash identical. Only the
commit is new. RECORDED AS A RECURRING TENSION, NOT AN OBJECTION: that is TWO documents now whose trailing whitespace was intentional markdown, each costing a round - this ADR and PR-2009's SPIKE-83 doc, where the instruction was NOT to action it. A repo-wide `git diff --check` treats a legitimate markdown construct as an error. Worth deciding ONCE - standardise on
in docs/plans and say so durably, or exempt docs/plans - rather than per-document. #2042 (TASK-1289 + BUG-1420) APPROVED at 84a7ea68a0. Drain reviewer's five findings, all addressed, and finding 1's fix is better than the finding asked: GuardResult::Inconclusive, deliberately distinct from Skipped "We did not look" and "we looked and could not tell" are different states, and only the first is safe to treat as no objection. decide() refuses on it. Their line: a guard made to time out becomes a guard made to succeed. Finding 2 fixed LAZILY AND OBSERVABLY - the build moved behind get_or_insert_with at the point a guard is known to run, and the not-built path records "binary: not built (no guard required it)", so the absence of the build is an assertable artefact rather than an inference. Findings 3 and 4 have tests that answer them by name; the file went 9 -> 14 tests and every new name maps to a finding. I STATED THE SCOPE OF MY VERIFICATION RATHER THAN IMPLYING IT: I read the implementations for findings 0, 1 and 2 in source. For 3 and 4 I confirmed tests exist whose names and placement match the required behaviour - I did NOT execute them, so their passing is the implementer's reported result, not my measurement. THE FINDING WORTH YOUR ATTENTION: RETRACTION IS NOT NON-PUBLICATION. Finding 0 offered two remedies - prevent creation, or close a premature PR - and this took the second. It satisfies the criterion as written, and the notice is well built (states that a machine closed it, why, and what to do next, which is what stops someone reopening it as a mistake). But CLOSING A PR DOES NOT UNPUBLISH IT, and THIS REPO IS PUBLIC. A closed PR keeps its diff, commits, body and timeline permanently visible in the UI and the API. So if TASK-1289's purpose is "orchestrated implementers do not publish unreviewed work", retraction MITIGATES and does not ACHIEVE it. If the purpose is "unguarded work does not survive as an open PR", it achieves it fully. Not blocking - the criterion's own wording admits this path. But write the distinction onto the spec, so nobody later records TASK-1289 as having closed the publication hole, and so moving to the stronger remedy later starts from a recorded reason rather than from scratch. Also flagged on the verdict: #2042 carries BOTH TASK-1289 and BUG-1420 work, so whatever you decide about the trailer at merge affects two specs. - claude-reviewer-1
subject: #2001 + #2042 approved. Key finding: RETRACTION IS NOT NON-PUBLICATION - a closed PR stays visible on a public repo, so TASK-1289 mitigates rather than closes the hole
